blocks.text: This report provides a description of the manufacturing process for OCU400 (AAV5-hNR2E3) and summarizes the results for all the Drug Substance (DS) and Drug Product (DP) lots manufactured at CanSino Bio starting from GLP to PPQ batches. The Drug Substance manufacturing process comprises of upstream and downstream operations. The upstream process includes cell culture expansion, plasmid transfection, AAV production in cells, and cell harvest. The downstream process consists of cell lysis, Benzonase/Biolonase-mediated DNA digestion, depth filtration, Capto AVB affinity chromatography, density gradient ultracentrifugation, subsequent concentration and sterile filtration to produce the final bulk drug substance. The Drug Product process includes thawing, formulation of the drug substance, sterile filtration, aseptic filling, inspection, labeling, and storage. Release testing of OCU400 DS and DP batches from GLP to PPQ demonstrated that all quality attributes met established specifications, confirming that all lots are suitable for release and subsequent regulatory approval.

blocks.text: 2.1. Overview of Manufacturing Process for OCU400 (AAV5- hNR2E3) Drug Substance

The OCU400 drug substance (DS) manufacturing process consists of upstream cell expansion, transient transfection, harvest and lysis, clarification, purification, concentration, and formulation steps performed under specified GLP/GMP conditions. The process is scalable and applicable across clinical, engineering, validation, and commercial manufacturing batches.

The HEK293 cells are expanded through a stepwise scale-up in shake flasks and subsequently transferred to a production bioreactor. The manufacturing process utilizes a Working Cell Bank (WCB) derived from a well-characterized Master Cell Bank (MCB) prepared and qualified under GMP conditions (Refer the MCB and WCB characterization report: ERPT-0150).

Upon reaching the target cell density in the production bioreactor, the suspension culture is transiently transfected with a plasmid mixture containing the expression plasmid encoding hNR2E3, the AAV rep2/cap5 plasmid, and the adenoviral helper plasmid. The plasmids are manufactured from qualified bacterial cell banks and purified using chromatography-based methods prior to formulation in an appropriate buffer. The plasmid mixture is complexed with cationic lipid polyethylenimine (PEI) in Balan CD HEK293 media and added into the bioreactor. The culture is maintained under controlled conditions to allow AAV production.

Following the production phase, the culture is harvested, and the cell biomass is collected by centrifugation. The cell pellet is resuspended in lysis buffer and subjected to controlled freeze-thaw processing to generate cell lysate. The lysate is treated with nuclease to degrade host cell DNA and residual plasmid DNA.

rows: Consolidated Process Description and Batch Summary Report for OCU400 (AAV5-hNR2E3)

blocks.text: The treated lysate is clarified by centrifugation followed by depth filtration and bioburden reduction filtration. The clarified lysate is tested for vector genome (Vg) titer and subsequently purified using Capto AVB column for affinity purification. This column contains 14 kDa antibody expressed in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, which binds to AAV5. The AAV5-hNR2E3 viral particles bound to the Capto AVB column are eluted with elution buffer. The affinity-purified eluate is concentrated by tangential flow filtration. To separate full capsids from empty capsids and other impurities, the material is further purified by iodixanol density gradient ultracentrifugation. The fraction containing full AAV5-hNR2E3 viral particles is collected and pooled. The pooled fractions are concentrated by tangential flow filtration followed by diafiltration using DS buffer. Following final sterile filtration, the OCU400 bulk drug substance (BDS) is filled in sterile SEBC bottles and stored at ≤- 60℃. The production of the OCU400 DS at manufacturing scale is summarized in Figure 2.

blocks.text: 4. DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE UPSTREAM MANUFACTURING PROCESS
4.1. Overview of the Upstream Manufacturing Process

The OCU400 DS is produced in HEK293 suspension cell culture using a production bioreactor-based manufacturing process. HEK293 cells are initially recovered and cultivated in an Erlenmeyer shake flask to initiate the seed train. The cell culture is expanded from the HEK293SF-3F6 working cell bank (WCB) and is performed through sequential scale-up of the culture volume. Following recovery, the cells are expanded through progressively larger shake flask cultures and intermediate seed expansion steps until the required cell biomass is achieved for inoculation of the production bioreactor. The upstream process is designed to support manufacturing across campaigns while maintaining consistent culture conditions and process performance. The upstream process flow for OCU400 production from GLP to PPQ scale is represented in Figure 3.

blocks.text: 4.2. Production of Plasmids (Transgene, Helper, and Rep/Cap)

The production of OCU400 (AAV5-hNR2E3) is based on triple plasmid transfection in HEK293 suspension cells with transgene phNR2E3, pRep2/Cap5, and pHelper plasmids. The phNR2E3 transgene plasmid is designed, synthesized, and characterized for identity and integrity of various regulatory elements (AAV2-ITR, CMV enhancer, CBA promoter, chimeric intron from rabbit globulin gene, and SV40 poly A). The rep gene sequence consists of wild type AAV2 serotype, and the cap gene sequence consists of wild type AAV5 serotype. The pHelper plasmid is used to provide various factors for AAV5 production in HEK293 cells. During research and development, Ampicillin antibiotic cassette was replaced with a kanamycin antibiotic cassette in all the plasmids (phNR2E3, pRep2/Cap5 and pHelper plasmids) and characterized for identity in plasmids produced during cGMP production. The purified plasmids were released against the specification.
4.3.1. Overview of Seed Flask Preparation and Inoculation

The purpose of the seed flask passage steps is to generate sufficient biomass of HEK293 cells for inoculation in the production bioreactor. Seed cultures are passaged at defined intervals under controlled conditions to maintain cell viability and growth characteristics. Subsequent seed flasks are inoculated at an appropriate viable cell density to support consistent expansion. Cells are sequentially expanded through culturing in a series of shake flasks and transferred to a seed bioreactor to generate adequate cell biomass for inoculation of the production bioreactor. The seed train strategy is scalable and designed to ensure consistent cell growth performance across manufacturing scales.

OCU400 is produced using the HEK293SF-3F6 Working Cell Bank (WCB), which is derived from a well-characterized HEK293 Master Cell Bank (MCB) established under applicable conditions. The Master and Working Cell Banks have been prepared, qualified, and fully characterized in accordance with regulatory expectations to ensure identity, purity, safety, and suitability for manufacturing use.

The vials of the HEK293SF-3F6 Working Cell Bank (WCB) are taken from liquid nitrogen storage and thawed in a water bath at 37±1℃ for 2-5 minutes. The thawed vials are transferred to a biosafety cabinet. Within the biosafety cabinet, pre-warmed SFM Transfx- 293 medium is transferred into a sterile centrifuge tube, and the thawed HEK293SF-3F6

The transfection process is performed in the production bioreactor and is designed to be scalable across manufacturing campaigns. Critical process parameters are maintained consistently to ensure robust performance during scale-up. blocks.text: The production bioreactor culture is collected into sterile centrifuge bottles and centrifuged for a specified time at 2-8℃ for harvesting. The cell pellet are resuspended with lysis buffer stored at ≤-60℃ for ≥ 72 hours. Frozen cell harvests are thawed in water bath at 37 ± 1 ℃ and treated with biolonase to digest host cell DNA and plasmid DNA. After conductivity adjustment with IEX buffer, the crude cell lysate is clarified by centrifugation and depth filtration and further processed using a 0.65/0.2-micron filter to reduce bioburden. The clarified lysate is purified using Capto AVB affinity chromatography in a bind and elute mode. OCU400 (AAV5-hNR2E3) is eluted at low pH, the eluate was concentrated by TFF (TFF-1) and further purified by density gradient ultra-centrifugation. OCU400 (AAV5- hNR2E3) is collected and concentrated to a designated viral particle concentration (Vg) by TFF (TFF-2) and formulated by diafiltration with the formulation buffer. Each bottle is rinsed with lysis buffer, and an additional lysis buffer is added as needed to achieve a final lysate weight per bottle. The pooled lysate is stored at ≤-60℃ for ≥ 72 hours. A Vg test is performed on all in-process samples.

blocks.text: After an initial WFI rinse, the Capto AVB column is sanitized with 0.5 M sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solution. The column is washed with a defined column volume (CV) of WFI followed by equilibration with defined column volume (CV) of AVB Equilibration buffer. AVB loading bag is removed from 2 to 8 ℃ storage and loaded onto the column at a specified flow rate.

The flow-through is collected in a storage bag starting at A280 of ≥10.0 mAU and ending at 50.0 mAU. Samples of the flow-through is collected for Vg titer testing and kept frozen at ≤ - 60℃. The column is re-equilibrated with a defined column volume (CV) of AVB Equilibration at a specified flow rate. The column is washed with a defined column volume (CV) of Wash Buffer, at a specified flow rate.

The viral particles are eluted with Elution Buffer into a SEBC bottle containing 2 M Tris buffer. Collection is initiated at A280 5 to 10 mAU and ending at A 280 20 to 10 mAU at a specified flow rate. The pH of the eluate is adjusted to 7.80 to 8.20 with 2 M Tris buffer (pH 9.00±0.05). Samples were collected from the eluate and frozen at ≤-60℃ for Vg titer testing. The remainder of the eluate is transferred to 2 to 8℃ storage. The column is washed with AVB Equilibration buffer followed by WFI and stored in 20% ethanol.

blocks.text: 5.6.1. Overview of concentration of Capto AVB Eluate (TFF-1)

The AVB eluate is concentrated using TFF. The TFF system is equipped with a Hollow fiber 100kDa mPES membrane. Prior to use, the module is rinsed with WFI and sanitized with 0.5M NaOH. The base is washed out by an additional WFI rinse followed by equilibration in the AVB Equilibration Buffer. The Capto AVB eluate is concentrated to 0.5-1.0 × 1013 Vg/mL.
5.6.2. Process Description: Concentration of Capto AVB Eluate (TFF-1)

A hollow fiber filter is installed to the tangential flow filtration (TFF) system. A feed tube, retentate tube, and permeate tube are cyclically rinsed with WFI, determine the dead volume and perform integrity testing. The filter is cleaned with 0.5 M NaOH. The filter is then rinsed with WFI until the permeate liquid reaches close to pH of WFI. The filter is equilibrated with AVB equilibration buffer. The retentate tube and hollow fiber are drained and pH of permeate solution is determined (Table 30).

The Vg titer results of the eluate are recorded, and the eluate is concentrated to a target of 0.5 to 1 × 1013 Vg/mL Ultrafiltration is performed to concentrate the eluate. The retentate tube and hollow fiber are drained, and the permeation is collected in a SEBC bottle, and the weight is recorded.

The membrane is washed with AVB Equilibration Buffer, and the wash solution is collected in a storage bottle. Wash solution and concentrated virus particles are transferred into a storage bottle. Sample is collected and frozen at ≤ -60℃ for Vg titer testing. Final concentrated virus solution is stored at 2 to 8℃.

5.7.1. Overview of iodixanol density ultracentrifugation step

Density gradient ultracentrifugation with iodixanol is used to separate the empty capsids from full capsids. The TFF-1 concentrate is divided into multiple centrifuge tubes and centrifuged for 80 to 100 minutes. The tubes are punctured at the bottom, and an additional syringe is inserted at the top to force liquid downward. The first liquid portion of the tube is discarded, after which fractions are collected containing the full viral particles. These fractions are pooled from the centrifuge tubes and tested for Vg titer. The product is either frozen or used for the TFF-2 step for concentration and diafiltration using the formulation buffer.

The bottles of TFF-1 concentrate are removed from the 2 to 8℃ storage <24 hours, and 17.0 to 18.0 mL of concentrate is added into each of 8 ultracentrifugation tubes followed by sequential addition of different percentages of iodixanol solutions as depicted in Figure 5 .

PBS (1X) is added to fill the remaining volume in the tube, and the tube opening is heat sealed. Tubes are centrifuged at 69,000 rpm for 80 to 100 minutes at 16 to 20℃. Following ultracentrifugation, an 18G syringe needle is inserted in the bottom of the tube to create an opening, and a single use venoclysis needle (0.55×17.5RWLB) is inserted in the top of the tube. Air is injected into the tube to force the liquid to flow downward. The first 2.5 mL solution is discarded, and a 2.5 mL solution containing the viral particles is collected

blocks.text: 5.8. TFF-2: Concentration of Pooled Ultrafiltration Samples and Buffer Exchange
5.8.1. Overview of concentration of Pooled Ultrafiltration Samples and Buffer Exchange

The ultrafiltration (UF) pool is concentrated using TFF system equipped with a Hollow fiber 100kDa mPES membrane. Prior to use, the module is rinsed with WFI and sanitized with NaOH. The base is washed out by an additional WFI rinse, followed by equilibration in Formulation Buffer. The UF pool is concentrated to a 0.5-2.0 × 1013 Vg titer and diafiltered using DS Buffer.
5.8.2. Process Description: Concentration of Pooled Ultrafiltration Samples and Buffer Exchange

A hollow fiber filter is installed to the TFF system. A feed tube, retentate tube, and permeate tube are cyclically rinsed with WFI, determine the dead volume (≤150.0g) and perform integrity testing. The filter is cleaned with 0.5 M NaOH and then rinsed with WFI until the permeate liquid reaches close to pH of WFI. The system is then equilibrated with DS Buffer (1.8mM sodium dihydrogen phosphate, 8.2mM disodium hydrogen phosphate, 180 mM sodium chloride, and 0.001% Poloxamer 188), pH of permeate rinsing solution should be 7.30±0.05.
Based on the result of the Vg titer test, the diluted viral particle solution is concentrated via ultrafiltration to the target viral particle concentration of 0.5-2.0× 1013 Vg/mL.

The concentrated viral particle solution is diluted 30 times with DS buffer, and diafiltration is performed for buffer exchange at a defined flow rate and TMP . The membrane is circulated with 1.0-1.5 DV of DS Buffer (wash volume for Phase1/2), and the solution added to the viral concentrate. Samples are taken for Vg titer testing and frozen at ≤ -60℃. The concentrated and purified OCU400 is stored at 2 to 8℃ for less than 24 hours.

6. DESCRIPTION OF AND COMPOSITION OF OCU400 (AAV5- HNR2E3) DRUG PRODUCT

OCU400 (AAV5-hNR2E3) drug product (DP) is a clear, colorless, sterile solution containing AAV5-hNR2E3 at a target concentration of 2.1 × 1012 vg/mL. DP is formulated in 10 mM sodium phosphate, 180 mM sodium chloride, and 0.001% Poloxamer 188 (PF-68), pH 7.3±0.5.

OCU400 is administered as a single dose through the subretinal route of administration. OCU400 (AAV5-hNR2E3) DP is provided as 0.6 mL in 2 mL Crystal Zenith® (CZ) vials. A kit containing one vial of DP and three vials of vehicle (formulation buffer or diluent) will be packaged together and supplied to approved hospitals/clinical centers at ≤ -60℃.

blocks.text: Overall, the evaluation of OCU400 DS and DP manufacturing performance across all the batches demonstrated:
· Consistent execution of the manufacturing process.
· Acceptable control of critical process parameters.
· Drug substance and drug product meeting predefined release specifications.

Comparative yield across all the batches (Table 21), in-process data (Table 19), and release testing results (Table 46-49) indicates that the manufacturing process is robust, reproducible, and capable of consistently producing OCU400 DS and DP that meet predefined quality requirements. The manufacturing process implemented for all the OCU400 DS and DP production, demonstrated adequate process control and batch-to-batch consistency across the evaluated manufacturing campaigns. Based on the available manufacturing, analytical, and process performance data from the GLP, engineering, GMP, and PPQ batches, the manufacturing process for the OCU400 DS and DP is considered suitable for routine commercial manufacturing and capable of consistently producing material meeting predefined quality attributes and specifications.
